tools.name: start-sms-verification
tools.description: Start an SMS OTP verification for a phone number (E.164). Use when the user wants to *verify* ownership of a number via a one-time code. After success, ask them for the OTP and call report-sms-verification. Do NOT use number-lookup (carrier/line info) or send-text-message (arbitrary SMS content) for phone number ownership verification flows.

phoneNumber.description: Phone number in E.164 format to send the SMS to

tools.name: report-sms-verification
tools.description: Report the received verification code to verify it, using the phone number of the user

phoneNumber.description: Phone number in E.164 format used to start the verification process

oneTimePassword.description: The code which was received by the user submitting the SMS verification.

tools.name: number-lookup
tools.description: Look up line/carrier information for a phone number (E.164) via Number Lookup — validity, type, and related metadata. Use when the user asks whether a number is valid or what carrier/type it is. Do NOT use this for RCS device feature support (use get-rcs-number-capabilities), SMS verification codes (use start-sms-verification), or searching Sinch virtual numbers to rent (use search-for-available-numbers).

phoneNumber.description: Phone number in E.164 format to look up

tools.name: send-text-message
tools.description: Send a text message to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.

recipient.description: (Required) The recipient to send the message to. This can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel such as Messenger.

channel.description: (Required) The channel to use for sending the message.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

sender.description: (Optional) The phone number of the message's sender (E.164 format). If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "DEFAULT_SMS_ORIGINATOR".

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: send-media-message
tools.description: Send a media message from URL given in parameter to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel. The media must be specified with its URL.

recipient.description: (Required) The recipient to send the message to. This can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel such as Messenger.

url.description: The URL of the media that will be the content of the message.

channel.description: (Required) The channel to use for sending the message.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

sender.description: (Optional) The phone number of the message's sender (E.164 format). If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "DEFAULT_SMS_ORIGINATOR".

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: send-location-message
tools.description: Send a location message from an address given in parameter to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.

recipient.description: (Required) The recipient to send the message to. This can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel such as Messenger.

lat.description: Latitude; used only when long and title are also provided.

long.description: Longitude; used only when lat and title are also provided.

title.description: Shown close to the button or link that leads to a map showing the location; used only when lat and long are also provided (the geocoded address is used instead when the address field is set).

label.description: Label or name for the position.

address.description: Address to geocode into latitude/longitude coordinates.
It can either be the plain text address that will be converted into latitude /longitude or directly the latitude / longitude coordinates if the user wants to send a specific location.

channel.description: (Required) The channel to use for sending the message.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

sender.description: (Optional) The phone number of the message's sender (E.164 format). If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "DEFAULT_SMS_ORIGINATOR".

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: send-choice-message
tools.description: Send a choice message to the user. The choice message can contain up to 3 choices if not text or up to 10 message if text only. Each choice can be a call message (phone number + title to display next to it), a location message (latitude / longitude + title to display next to it), a text message or a URL message (the URL to click on + title to display next to it). The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.

recipient.description: (Required) The recipient to send the message to. This can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel such as Messenger.

items.description: Choice message that can be a call, location, text, or URL. Exactly one must be provided. The "title" parameter must not be provided is case of text choice.

choiceContent.description: The list of choices to send to the user

text.description: The text to be sent along the choice array

mediaUrl.description: The media URL to be sent along the choice array

channel.description: (Required) The channel to use for sending the message.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

sender.description: (Optional) The phone number of the message's sender (E.164 format). If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "DEFAULT_SMS_ORIGINATOR".

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: send-template-message
tools.description: Send an omni-template message (referred by template ID, ULID) to a contact on the specified channel. The contact can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel.

recipient.description: (Required) The recipient to send the message to. This can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel such as Messenger.

templateId.description: The ID (ULID format) of the omni-template template to use for sending the message.

language.description: The language to use for the omni-template (BCP-47). If not set, the default language code will be used.

parameters.description: The parameters to use for the template. This is a key-value map where the key is the parameter name and the value is the parameter value. Look carefully in the prompt to find which parameters are expected by the template.

channel.description: (Required) The channel to use for sending the message.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

sender.description: (Optional) The phone number of the message's sender (E.164 format). If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "DEFAULT_SMS_ORIGINATOR".

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: send-whatsapp-template-message
tools.description: Send a WhatsApp-native template message (referred by template name) to a contact (phone number in E.164 format) on the WhatsApp channel. For omni-channel templates use send-template-message instead.

recipient.description: (Required) The recipient to send the message to. This can be a phone number in E.164 format, or the identifier for the specified channel such as Messenger.

templateName.description: The name of the template to use for sending the message on WhatsApp specifically.

templateLanguage.description: The language to use for the WhatsApp template (BCP-47).

parameters.description: Template variable values, keyed using WhatsApp's structured parameter format: <component>[<index>]<subtype>[<paramIndex>]<field>, e.g. "body[1]text" or "button[0]url[1]text". component is header, body, button, or carousel; index is 0-based and only used for carousel cards and buttons (omit it for header/body); paramIndex is 1-based. Never use bare keys like "1" or dotted keys like "body.1" — WhatsApp does not recognize them and the send will silently fail. Examples: "body[1]text" for a body variable; "header[1]text" for a text header variable; "header[1]image.link" / "header[1]video.link" / "header[1]document.link" (+ optional "header[1]document.filename") for a media header; "header[1]location.latitude" and "header[1]location.longitude" (+ optional "header[1]location.name" / "header[1]location.address") for a location header; "button[0]quick_reply[1]payload", "button[0]url[1]text", "button[0]copy_code[1]coupon_code", "button[0]flow[1]action.type" for interactive buttons; "carousel[0]header[1]image.link" and "carousel[0]body[1]text" for carousel card content.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

sender.description: (Optional) The phone number of the message's sender (E.164 format). If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "DEFAULT_SMS_ORIGINATOR".

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

metadata.description: Custom data to send along with the message (e.g. correlation IDs, appointment IDs, etc.)

tools.name: list-conversation-apps
tools.description: Get a list of all Conversation apps in the account. Apps are created and configured in the Sinch Dashboard or with the Conversation API. The App is the entity that holds the credentials related to the various channels

tools.name: create-conversation-app
tools.description: Create a new Conversation API app in the project. No channels are configured at creation; use set-sms-channel-on-app, set-rcs-channel-on-app, or set-whatsapp-channel-on-app to configure channels later. Read the conversation-app-setup resource for the full flow.

displayName.description: Display name for the Conversation API app.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: update-conversation-app
tools.description: Update a Conversation API app display name. To configure or replace channel credentials, use set-sms-channel-on-app, set-rcs-channel-on-app, or set-whatsapp-channel-on-app instead.

appId.description: The Conversation API app ID. Use list-conversation-apps to find existing app IDs.

displayName.description: New display name for the Conversation API app.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: delete-conversation-app
tools.description: Delete a Conversation API app by its ID. This permanently removes the app and its channel configuration.

appId.description: The Conversation API app ID. Use list-conversation-apps to find existing app IDs.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: set-sms-channel-on-app
tools.description: Set (create or replace) the SMS channel on a Conversation API app. Requires the SMS service plan ID and API token. The app must be in the same region as the SMS service plan. To rename an app, use update-conversation-app instead. For vague requests such as "add messaging", ask whether the user means SMS, RCS, or WhatsApp and collect the required credentials before calling a tool.

appId.description: The Conversation API app ID. Use list-conversation-apps to find existing app IDs.

apiToken.description: Sinch API token for the SMS service plan.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: set-rcs-channel-on-app
tools.description: Set (create or replace) the RCS channel on a Conversation API app. Requires the RCS sender ID and bearer token. To rename an app, use update-conversation-app instead. For vague requests such as "add messaging", ask whether the user means SMS, RCS, or WhatsApp and collect the required credentials before calling a tool.

appId.description: The Conversation API app ID. Use list-conversation-apps to find existing app IDs.

senderId.description: Claimed identity for the RCS channel — use the `authName` field from get-rcs-sender/create-rcs-sender. Do NOT use the sender's `id`; that is a different identifier and will cause the channel to fail or disappear from the app.

bearerToken.description: Bearer token for the RCS channel — use the `authToken` field from get-rcs-sender/create-rcs-sender. Do NOT use `authName` here; it looks similar but belongs in `senderId`, not `bearerToken`.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: set-whatsapp-channel-on-app
tools.description: Set (create or replace) the WhatsApp channel on a Conversation API app. Requires the WhatsApp sender ID and bearer token. To rename an app, use update-conversation-app instead. For vague requests such as "add messaging", ask whether the user means SMS, RCS, or WhatsApp and collect the required credentials before calling a tool.

appId.description: The Conversation API app ID. Use list-conversation-apps to find existing app IDs.

bearerToken.description: Bearer token for the WhatsApp channel.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: list-messaging-templates
tools.description: Get a list of the omni-channel messaging templates (managed by Sinch) belonging to an account, for the configured region only. Note that this list does NOT include: (1) Email templates - use the list-email-templates tool to fetch them; (2) WhatsApp channel-specific templates (managed by Meta) - use the list-whatsapp-templates tool to fetch them. If the user asks for all their messaging templates, you can propose to additionally call list-whatsapp-templates to fetch the WhatsApp-specific templates.

tools.name: list-webhooks
tools.description: List all webhooks configured for a Conversation app. Webhooks receive Conversation API callbacks at a target URL when selected triggers occur. Configure signing secrets in the Sinch Dashboard.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: get-webhook
tools.description: Get a Conversation API webhook by its ID. Signing secrets are not returned — configure them in the Sinch Dashboard. Use list-webhooks to browse webhooks when the user does not have an ID yet.

webhookId.description: (Required) The ID of the webhook. You can obtain it from list-webhooks or the Sinch Dashboard.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: create-webhook
tools.description: Create a webhook for a Conversation app (up to 5 per app). Events are delivered to the target URL over HTTP when triggers fire. Configure the signing secret in the Sinch Dashboard; it is not set through this tool.

target.description: (Required) The HTTPS URL where Conversation API events should be delivered. Maximum length is 742 characters.

appId.description: (Optional) The ID of the app to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable "CONVERSATION_APP_ID".

triggers.description: (Optional) Event triggers that activate this webhook. Omit to leave without triggers, or pass an empty array [] to clear all triggers on update. Use update-webhook to add triggers later.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: update-webhook
tools.description: Update an existing Conversation API webhook. Provide at least one of target or triggers. Signing secrets are configured in the Sinch Dashboard, not through this tool.

webhookId.description: (Required) The ID of the webhook. You can obtain it from list-webhooks or the Sinch Dashboard.

target.description: (Optional) The HTTPS URL where Conversation API events should be delivered.

triggers.description: (Optional) Event triggers that activate this webhook. Omit to leave without triggers, or pass an empty array [] to clear all triggers on update. Use update-webhook to add triggers later.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: delete-webhook
tools.description: Permanently delete a Conversation API webhook by its ID. Ask for the webhook ID if missing. Prefer update-webhook to clear triggers if the user only wants to disable events.

webhookId.description: (Required) The ID of the webhook. You can obtain it from list-webhooks or the Sinch Dashboard.

region.description: (Optional) The region to use for the Sinch conversation API. If set, it will override the value from the environment variable CONVERSATION_REGION. Ignored when the deployment pins the region to its own configuration.

tools.name: tts-callout
tools.description: Place an outbound voice call that speaks a text-to-speech message when answered and returns a session ID. A session contains one or more call legs; use get-session-information to retrieve their call IDs and states. Use when the user wants to call a phone number and say something aloud. Do NOT use send-text-message for this. Requires phoneNumber and message; the caller ID is optional.

phoneNumber.description: The destination phone number in E.164 format, for example +14155550123

from.description: The active Sinch Voice number to call from, in E.164 format. Uses CALLING_LINE_IDENTIFICATION when omitted; if neither is set, the call has no caller ID.

message.description: The text or SSML message to read when the call is answered

voiceName.description: The Sinch TTS voice name. Defaults to Emma.

format.description: The message format. Defaults to TEXT.

serviceId.description: The Voice service ID. Uses the project default service when omitted.

dialTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for an answer. Defaults to 30.

maxCallDurationSeconds.description: Maximum call duration in seconds. Defaults to 300.

tools.name: get-call-information
tools.description: Get status and details for one voice call leg by call ID. A call is one leg within a session: use get-session-information first when you have the session ID returned by tts-callout or obtained from a batch. Do not use this to place a call or send an SMS.

callId.description: The voice call ID (not a session ID)

tools.name: list-calls
tools.description: List and filter voice call legs by service, endpoints, channel, time range, result, or reason. Results are returned one page at a time with pagination metadata.

serviceId.description: Only include calls for this Voice service ID

from.description: Only include calls from this origin

to.description: Only include calls to this destination

callType.description: Only include calls using this channel type

startTime.description: Only include calls started at or after this ISO 8601 datetime

endTime.description: Only include calls ended before this ISO 8601 datetime

callResult.description: Only include calls with this result

callReason.description: Only include calls with this completion reason

pageSize.description: The number of calls to return on this page

tools.name: get-session-information
tools.description: Get voice session details by session ID, including the call IDs and state of every call leg in the session. Sessions are returned directly by tts-callout or as part of a batch. Use get-call-information with a returned call ID to inspect one leg.

tools.name: create-voice-service
tools.description: Create a Voice service. Optionally add a description or make it the project default.

description.description: An optional description of the Voice service

isDefault.description: Set to true to make this the project default Voice service

tools.name: set-voice-service-webhook
tools.description: Set the primary webhook URL and fallback URL for a Voice service. This replaces its current call behavior with webhook handling.

serviceId.description: The UUID of the Voice service to update

url.description: The primary HTTP(S) webhook URL for Voice events

tools.name: remove-voice-service-webhook
tools.description: Remove webhook configuration from a Voice service, leaving it with no incoming-call behavior.

serviceId.description: The UUID of the Voice service whose webhook configuration should be removed

tools.name: assign-number-to-voice-service
tools.description: Assign an active Sinch number to a Voice service. The number must belong to the authenticated project and have Voice capability.

phoneNumber.description: The active Sinch number to assign, in E.164 format

serviceId.description: The UUID of the Voice service to assign the number to

tools.name: tts-batch-callout
tools.description: Create a batch of outbound voice calls that all play the same text-to-speech message. Accepts 1-500 E.164 destinations and returns a batch ID; each destination creates a session, and each session contains one or more call legs. Use get-voice-batch-summary to retrieve the session IDs for the batch. The caller ID is optional.

destinations.description: Destination numbers in E.164 format. This tool accepts at most 500 recipients per request to keep MCP payloads manageable.

from.description: The active Sinch Voice number to call from, in E.164 format. Uses CALLING_LINE_IDENTIFICATION when omitted; if neither is set, the call has no caller ID.

message.description: The text or SSML message to read when the call is answered

voiceName.description: The Sinch TTS voice name. Defaults to Emma.

format.description: The message format. Defaults to TEXT.

serviceId.description: The Voice service ID. Uses the project default service when omitted.

dialTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds to wait for an answer. Defaults to 30.

maxCallDurationSeconds.description: Maximum call duration in seconds. Defaults to 300.

maxCps.description: Maximum batch initiation rate in calls per second

ttlSeconds.description: Seconds the platform may keep attempting to initiate queued calls

tools.name: get-voice-batch-summary
tools.description: Get the execution summary for an outbound voice-call batch by batch ID. Enable session details to return the ID and state of each session in the batch; then use get-session-information to retrieve the call legs in a session.

batchId.description: The ULID returned when the voice batch was created

includeSessionDetails.description: Also return each initiated session ID and its current state. Defaults to false.

tools.name: send-email
tools.description: Send an email to a recipient with a subject and body.

body.description: The body of the email. Can be text or HTML

template.description: The name of a template to use to render the email body. If provided, the body will be ignored.

templateVariables.description: Variables to use in the template.

domain.description: The domain to use for sending the email. It would override the domain provided in the environment variables.

tools.name: retrieve-email-info
tools.description: Retrieve the content of an email and the events that happened thanks to its ID

domain.description: The domain to use for retrieving the email. If defined, it will override the domain provided in the environment variable "MAILGUN_DOMAIN".

tools.name: list-email-templates
tools.description: Get a list of Email templates from Mailgun for a specific domain. Note that the Messaging templates (omni-channel or channel-specific such as WhatsApp) are NOT included in this list - they can be found with another tool: list-messaging-templates. Do not try to use this tool to list Messaging templates, it will not work.

domain.description: The domain to use for sending the email. It would override the domain provided in the environment variables.

tools.name: list-email-events
tools.description: Get a raw log of individual email events from Mailgun for a specific domain, not aggregated rates or totals — for those, use analytics-metrics instead. You can filter by event type and limit the number of results.

domain.description: (Optional) The Mailgun domain to fetch events for.

event.description: (Optional) Filter by event type (e.g., delivered, opened, failed).

beginSearchPeriod.description: (Optional) The beginning of the search time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z).

endSearchPeriod.description: (Optional) The end of the search time range in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z).

tools.name: analytics-metrics
tools.description: Get aggregated email analytics from Mailgun for an account, such as rates and counts, computed over a time range. Use this for questions about rates, percentages, or totals. For a raw log of individual email events, use list-email-events instead. All parameters are optional. You can filter by domain, metrics type and specify a time range. By default, it will return all metrics for all your domains for the last 7 days.

domain.description: (Optional) The Mailgun domain to fetch metrics for.

metrics.description: (Optional) The specific metrics to receive the stats for. If not provided, all metrics will be returned.

beginSearchPeriod.description: (Optional) The beginning of the search time range in RFC-2822 format (e.g., Mon, 02 Jun 2025 00:00:00 +0100).

endSearchPeriod.description: (Optional) The end of the search time range in RFC-2822 format (e.g., Mon, 09 Jun 2025 00:00:00 +0100).

tools.name: list-available-regions
tools.description: List countries/regions where Sinch virtual numbers are available to search and rent. Use when the user asks where they can buy numbers or which regions are offered. Optional filter by number types (MOBILE, LOCAL, TOLL_FREE). If the user later wants to find candidates in a region, they can follow up with search-for-available-numbers.

types.description: Only return regions for which numbers are provided with the given types: MOBILE, LOCAL or TOLL_FREE.

tools.name: list-rented-numbers
tools.description: List phone numbers already rented/active on this project. Optional filters: region, type, digit pattern, SMS/VOICE capability. Use this to see what you own — not to find numbers still available to buy (use search-for-available-numbers) and not to look up carrier/line type for an arbitrary number (use number-lookup).

regionCode.description: Region code to filter by. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the phone number. Example: US, GB or SE.

type.description: Number type to filter by. Options include, MOBILE, LOCAL or TOLL_FREE.

searchPattern.description: Sequence of digits to search for. If you prefer or need certain digits in sequential order, you can enter the sequence of numbers here. For example, `2020`.

patternPosition.description: Position of the search pattern. Options include START, END or CONTAINS. If you want the search pattern to be at the beginning of the phone number, select START. If you want it at the end, select END. If you want it to be anywhere in the phone number, select CONTAINS.

capability.description: Number capabilities to filter by SMS and/or VOICE.

size.description: Maximum number of phone numbers to return.

tools.name: rent-sinch-virtual-numbers
tools.description: Rent (activate) one or more known Sinch virtual phone numbers on the project. Requires specific E.164 numbers (with leading +) that the user already chose — typically after search-for-available-numbers. Do NOT invent phone numbers. Do NOT use this to search or browse available numbers — use search-for-available-numbers for that. If the user has not provided an exact number, ask for it or search first.

numbers.description: Array of phone numbers to rent. Each number should be in E.164 format with leading `+`

tools.name: release-rented-number
tools.description: Release (cancel) a rented virtual phone number from the project. Requires the exact E.164 phone number. Ask for the number if missing. This is not for searching or renting numbers.

phoneNumber.description: The phone number in E.164 format with leading `+`

tools.name: get-rented-number-configuration
tools.description: Get a rented Sinch number by its exact E.164 phone number, including its metadata, capabilities, and current service configuration. Provisioning updates are asynchronous: while an update is pending, its future configuration and status appear in the corresponding `scheduled*Provisioning` property.

phoneNumber.description: The rented Sinch phone number to retrieve, in E.164 format with a leading `+`

tools.name: search-for-available-numbers
tools.description: Search for available Sinch virtual phone numbers you can rent (activate) later. Use this when the user wants to find or browse numbers (by country/region, type LOCAL/MOBILE/TOLL_FREE, area-code pattern, or SMS/VOICE capability) but has not yet chosen a specific E.164 number to activate. Do NOT use this to activate/rent a known number — use rent-sinch-virtual-numbers for that. If the user asks vaguely for "a support line" or "a number" without region/type, ask for country/region (and optionally area code or capabilities) before calling, or call this tool once those filters are clear.

regionCode.description: Region code to filter by. ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the phone number. Example: US, GB or SE.

type.description: Number type to filter by. Options include, MOBILE, LOCAL or TOLL_FREE.

searchPattern.description: Sequence of digits to search for. If you prefer or need certain digits in sequential order, you can enter the sequence of numbers here. For example, `2020`.

tools.name: launch-rcs-sender
tools.description: Submit an RCS sender for Google and carrier review. Before calling this tool, verify ALL of the following are set via update-rcs-sender — the launch is rejected if any item is missing: (1) details.brand.name; (2) details.brand.logoUrl (JPEG/PNG, max 50 KB, 224×224 px); (3) details.brand.bannerUrl (JPEG/PNG, max 200 KB, 1440×448 px); (4) details.brand.privacyPolicyUrl; (5) details.brand.termsOfServiceUrl; (6) at least one of details.brand.phones or details.brand.emails; (7) details.countries with at least one supported country code; (8) details.questionnaire.general.answers — all fields; (9) details.questionnaire.verification.answers — all fields; (10) country-specific questionnaire section for each country in details.countries (e.g. questionnaire.gb for GB, questionnaire.us for US, questionnaire.fr for FR). Use get-rcs-sender to review current values before launching. If the launch is rejected, the response lists exactly which required details are still missing so they can be filled in and the launch retried.

tools.name: get-whatsapp-account
tools.description: Get the WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) for the project: state, WABA ID, business details, ban state and date, daily message limit, compatible regions, and the Insights / Direct Send flags. Note: the Meta quality rating is not part of the response.

tools.name: list-whatsapp-templates
tools.description: Get a list of the WhatsApp channel-specific message templates (submitted to and reviewed by Meta) belonging to a project. Note that the omni-channel messaging templates (managed by Sinch) are NOT included in this list - use the list-messaging-templates tool to fetch them. If the user asks for all their messaging templates, you can combine this tool with list-messaging-templates.

tools.name: create-whatsapp-template
tools.description: Create a WhatsApp message template in the project. Required fields: name, language, category. Provide details.components to define the content — it must include a BODY component. If status is SUBMIT (the default), the template is submitted for review immediately; if DRAFT, it is saved without validation for later editing.

language.description: Template language — typically one of the listed codes, but any value Meta accepts is allowed since this list may not cover every language Meta supports.

text.description: Text to show in the header. Can contain one header variable. Not required for draft.

example.description: Example for the header variable. Required if there is a variable in the text header.

url.description: Uploaded media file URL. Image: 8-bit RGB/RGBA JPEG or PNG, max 5MB. Video: H.264/AAC, single or no audio stream, 3GP or MP4, max 16MB. Document: PDF, max 100MB. Not required for draft.

mimeType.description: Optional mime type of the file if it cannot be determined from the file contents.

example.description: Header media example. Not required for draft.

anyOf.description: Template header. A LOCATION header takes no other fields; TEXT and media formats add their own.

text.description: Body text. Not required for draft.

examples.description: Examples for the body variables. Requires one example for each variable in the body text. If no variables are used, the examples are optional.

addSecurityRecommendation.description: Only valid if template category is AUTHENTICATION. Adds a security recommendation to the body. Defaults to false.

codeExpirationMinutes.description: Only valid if template category is AUTHENTICATION. If set, adds text detailing the code expiration time.

text.description: Text to display on the Flow button. Not required for draft.

flowId.description: Flow ID to launch when the button is pressed. Not required for draft.

navigateScreen.description: The unique ID of the first screen. Required for the Navigate action.

supportedApps.description: List of supported apps for the OTP button.

zeroTapTermsAccepted.description: Set to true to indicate that zero-tap authentication use is subject to the WhatsApp Business Terms of Service, and that it is your responsibility to ensure customers expect the code to be auto-filled when they choose to receive it via WhatsApp.

url.description: The url address. To make it dynamic, add {{1}} at the end of the url (e.g. https://www.my-website.com?name={{1}}), not inside the domain. Restricted domains: wa.me, whatsapp.com. Not required for draft.

example.description: Example of the full url with the dynamic value filled in. Required if the url contains {{1}}, e.g. https://www.my-website.com?name=john.
Uploaded media asset handle. Media assets are automatically cropped to a wide ratio based on the recipient device. Not required for draft.

text.description: Card body text. Supports variables. Not required for draft.

examples.description: Examples for the body variables. Requires one example for each variable in the body text.

buttons.description: Card buttons. Can be a mix of quick reply, phone number, and URL buttons. Not required for draft.

components.description: Components of the card: an image or video header asset, card body text, and up to two buttons. All cards in a template must have the same components. Not required for draft.

cards.description: Media cards. All cards defined on a template must have the same components. Only two cards need to be defined at creation — an approved template with two cards can send up to 10. Not required for draft.

components.description: List of components in the template. Must contain a BODY component and can only have one entry of each type. Not required for draft.

messageSendTtlSeconds.description: Template message delivery retry time-to-live override, in seconds. If unset, the message is retried for the category's default period before being dropped: AUTHENTICATION 600s (10 min), MARKETING 2592000s (30 days), UTILITY 2592000s (30 days). If overriding, valid ranges differ from the defaults: AUTHENTICATION 10-900 (10 sec-15 min), MARKETING 43200-2592000 (12 hours-30 days), UTILITY 30-43200 (30 sec-12 hours). Authentication templates created before 2024-10-23 default to a 30-day TTL.

saveDraftOnFailure.description: Save the template as a draft if submission fails. Defaults to false.

tools.name: delete-single-whatsapp-template-language
tools.description: Destructive — always ask the user to confirm the exact templateName and languageCode in chat and wait for an explicit yes before calling this tool. Delete ONE language variant of a WhatsApp message template, identified by templateName and languageCode — other language variants of this template name are left untouched. To delete every language variant of a template name at once, use delete-all-whatsapp-template-languages instead. By default only the draft is removed; set deleteSubmitted to also remove a template already submitted to Meta. The template name itself is not freed up by deletion — recreating a template with this same name and language is blocked for 30 days after an approved variant is deleted; update the submitted template instead if you need it again soon.

templateName.description: The unique name of the template.

languageCode.description: The language code of the specific template variant to delete — typically one of the listed codes, but any value Meta accepts is allowed since this list may not cover every language Meta supports. Other language variants of this template name are left untouched.

deleteSubmitted.description: Also delete the template already submitted to Meta, not just the draft. Defaults to false, which only deletes a draft and throws an error if the template has been submitted. Deleting an approved template does not free up its name — recreating a template with this same name and language is blocked for 30 days.

tools.name: delete-all-whatsapp-template-languages
tools.description: Destructive — always ask the user to confirm the exact templateName in chat and wait for an explicit yes before calling this tool. Delete ALL language variants of a WhatsApp message template by name, in one call — draft and submitted variants alike, regardless of state. This is more destructive than delete-single-whatsapp-template-language, which only removes a single language variant; use this one only when every language of the template name should be removed. This does not free up the name — recreating a template with this same name and any language it had approved is blocked for 30 days. In-flight messages already sent with the deleted template keep attempting delivery for 30 days.

templateName.description: The unique name of the template. Every language variant of this template name is deleted — to remove only one language, use delete-single-whatsapp-template-language instead.
